ic_name: HDMI / DVI TMDS (TI TFP410 PanelBus Digital Transmitter — subset)

protocol_overview.type: Source-synchronous, half-duplex (per pair), serial Transition-Minimized Differential Signaling (T.M.D.S.) protocol for DVI 1.0 / HDMI video. 3 data pairs + 1 clock pair. Per-pixel 8b/10b-style encoding; DC-balanced.
protocol_overview.duplex: Unidirectional per TMDS pair (source TX → sink RX); sideband DDC (I2C, bidirectional) carries EDID + HDCP traffic; HPD is sink → source.
wire_names: TX0+ / TX0- (Channel 0 — Blue / HSYNC+VSYNC in blanking)
TX1+ / TX1- (Channel 1 — Green / CTL[1] in blanking)
TX2+ / TX2- (Channel 2 — Red / CTL[3:2] in blanking)
protocol_overview.wire_count: 8 high-speed wires (4 differential pairs); + 2 sideband (SCL + SDA for DDC/I2C) + 1 HPD = 11 typical for full DVI/HDMI cable connection.
protocol_overview.dual_mode_signaling: TMDS only (no LP/HS dual-mode like MIPI). The TFP410 supports adjustable PHY swing 400-600 mV diff (R_TFADJ sets full-scale current).
protocol_overview.controller_role: Source (TFP410 + graphics controller) is the unique TMDS transmitter; drives pixel clock + 3 encoded data channels.
protocol_overview.target_role: Sink (display / TV / projector) recovers pixel clock from TXC and samples 3 data channels; decodes 10b → 8b RGB; drives HPD high to signal presence; serves EDID on DDC; participates in HDCP authentication (HDCP is system-level, not TFP410-internal).
protocol_overview.encoding_summary: Per pixel × channel: 8 input bits → 10 TMDS bits. Step 1: minimize transitions (XOR / XNOR over input + previous bit). Step 2: invert if needed to balance running DC count. The 10-bit symbol's bit-9 indicates inversion and bit-8 indicates XOR vs XNOR. Control characters (HSYNC/VSYNC/CTL) use 4 reserved 10-bit codes with max transitions (high transition density) so receivers can distinguish them from video data.

functional_requirements.text: TMDS interface shall have exactly 3 differential data pairs (TX0/TX1/TX2) plus 1 differential clock pair (TXC). 4 differential pairs total.

DE=high (active video): Channel 0 (TX0) carries Blue[7:0], Channel 1 (TX1) carries Green[7:0], Channel 2 (TX2) carries Red[7:0]. DE=low (blanking): Channel 0 carries HSYNC + VSYNC, Channel 1 carries CTL[1], Channel 2 carries CTL[3:2]. CTL3 reserved for HDCP and is always 0.

Pixel clock rate (IDCK / TXC frequency) shall be in the range 25 MHz to 165 MHz (DVI 1.0 single-link limit). Per-channel TMDS data rate = pixel rate × 10 bits/pixel × 1 sample-per-clock = 250 Mbps min to 1650 Mbps (≈ 1.65 Gbps) max per pair.

Each 8-bit input byte (R, G, or B) shall be encoded into a 10-bit T.M.D.S. character: stage-1 selects XOR or XNOR cascade to minimise transitions and emits bit-8 (operation flag) + 8 cascaded bits; stage-2 decides DC-balance inversion and emits bit-9 (inversion flag) over the cascaded 8 bits. Running disparity is maintained per channel.

Control characters (encoding {VSYNC, HSYNC}, {0,0}={0x354}, {0,1}={0x0AB}, {1,0}={0x154}, {1,1}={0x2AB} on Channel 0 only — high transition density; remaining channels use {CTL[1],0} / {CTL[3],CTL[2]} mappings) are transmitted on the inactive (blanking) interval to delimit video and synchronize the receiver.

CTL[3] is reserved for HDCP and is always encoded as 0 by TFP410. CTL[2:1] inputs may be driven by the host during DE=low and are encoded onto TX2 (CTL2) and TX1 (CTL1). When DE=high, CTL and SYNC pins must be held constant.

Input mode shall be either 24-bit single-edge (BSEL=1) — all 24 pixel bits latched on one clock edge — OR 12-bit dual-edge (BSEL=0) — 12 bits latched on each edge (LSB half on one edge, MSB half on the other). Selection by BSEL pin (ISEL=0) or CTL_1_MODE.BSEL bit (ISEL=1).
Input pixel clock IDCK shall be single-ended (CMOS IDCK+ with IDCK- tied to GND) OR fully differential (IDCK+ vs IDCK-). Differential mode is only available in low-swing mode (V_REF ≤ 0.9 V).

EDGE pin (ISEL=0) or CTL_1_MODE.EDGE (ISEL=1) selects primary latching edge: EDGE=1 → rising edge of IDCK+; EDGE=0 → falling edge of IDCK+. In 12-bit dual-edge mode, EDGE selects which half-pixel is latched on the rising edge.
V_REF selects input swing mode. V_REF=DV_DD (3.3 V) → high-swing 3.3 V CMOS inputs. V_REF=0.55..0.9 V → low-swing 1.1-1.8 V CMOS inputs; minimum input swing = V_REF ± 0.2 V.

Data de-skew shall be programmable when DKEN=1 (pin or register). DK[3:1] (3-bit code 000..111) selects 1 of 8 t_STEP increments (default DK[3:1]=100 = step 5). Skew = (DK[3:1] - 4) × t_STEP, range -4·t_STEP to +3·t_STEP. t_STEP = 350 ps per step. Sole purpose: compensate IDCK ↔ DATA setup/hold mismatch.

Power-down (PD active-low pin or CTL_1_MODE.PD register bit). PD=0 → only digital I/O buffers and I2C interface remain active; TMDS drivers, PLL, and encoders are gated off. PD=1 → normal operation. Default after RESET is PD=0 (powered down).

TFP410 includes an internal DE generator (DE_CTL.DE_GEN=1) that regenerates an active-video DE signal from HSYNC + VSYNC + DE_DLY (pixel offset after HSYNC) + DE_CNT (active line width) + DE_TOP (line offset after VSYNC) + DE_LIN (active line height). When DE_GEN=1, the external DE pin is ignored.

When ISEL=1, TFP410 is programmable via a standard 7-bit-address I2C target interface (SCL on pin 15, SDA on pin 14). A[3:1] address bits are pin-strapped to CTL3/CTL2/CTL1 pins; base 7-bit address = 0b0111_A3A2A1 (write addresses 0x70..0x7E even, read addresses 0x71..0x7F odd). Page mode not supported; byte read/write only.

The I2C interface in TFP410 also functions as a DDC (Display Data Channel) bridge to read EDID from the connected display. EDID device address (per DVI / VESA standard) = 0xA0 (write) / 0xA1 (read). HDCP device address (system-level) = 0x74 / 0x75. HDCP cipher itself is NOT implemented in TFP410 — only DDC transport is provided.

Hot-Plug Detect (HTPLG): when I2C is enabled (ISEL=1), the EDGE/HTPLG pin samples the receiver-supplied HPD signal (1 kΩ pull-down typical; receiver drives HIGH when connected and powered). HTPLG status is reflected in CTL_2_MODE.HTPLG; an interrupt can be generated on HTPLG change (TSEL bit selects RSEN or HTPLG as interrupt source).

Receiver Sense (RSEN): when ISEL=0, MSEN pin outputs HIGH if a powered receiver is detected (low-current sense on TX0+/TX0-). When ISEL=1, RSEN status is in CTL_2_MODE.RSEN and MSEN is programmable via MSEL[3:1].

VEN (VSYNC enable) and HEN (HSYNC enable) bits in CTL_1_MODE control whether the VSYNC and HSYNC inputs are transmitted in their original state (VEN/HEN=1) or are forced to fixed LOW (VEN/HEN=0) at the TMDS output.

ISEL/RST pin is bi-functional: ISEL=1 selects I2C mode; bringing ISEL low and back high asynchronously RESETs the I2C register file to default values. PD register defaults to 0 after RESET so the device is powered down until explicitly enabled via I2C.

TMDS output single-ended swing V_SWING shall be 400-600 mV (typ), set by external R_TFADJ resistor on TFADJ pin (R_TFADJ ≈ 510 Ω ± 1% gives 400-600 mV). Differential swing = 2 × V_SWING ≈ 800-1200 mV pp.

configurations.name: 24-bit single-edge, single-ended clock, high-swing (BSEL=1, V_REF=DV_DD)
configurations.description: Most common config; standard 3.3 V CMOS inputs, 24-bit pixel latched on rising or falling IDCK+ edge per EDGE; 25-165 MHz.

configurations.name: 12-bit dual-edge, single-ended clock, high-swing (BSEL=0, V_REF=DV_DD)
configurations.description: 12 pixel bits per clock edge; halves the data wires; 25-165 MHz pixel rate.

configurations.name: 24-bit single-edge, differential clock, low-swing (BSEL=1, V_REF=0.55-0.9V, DSEL=1)
configurations.description: Reduced-EMI low-swing input, differential pixel clock for better common-mode rejection.

configurations.name: 12-bit dual-edge, differential clock, low-swing (BSEL=0, V_REF=0.55-0.9V, DSEL=0)
configurations.description: Differential clock + dual-edge data + low-swing inputs; maximum noise margin.

configurations.name: Power-down (PD=0)
configurations.description: Only digital I/O buffers and I2C interface remain active; TMDS drivers, PLL, encoders gated.

configurations.name: DE-Generator enabled (DE_CTL.DE_GEN=1)
configurations.description: TFP410 regenerates DE from HSYNC + VSYNC + programmed offsets; the external DE pin is ignored.

error_response_conditions: Pixel clock outside 25-165 MHz — PLL fails to lock; TMDS output gated; receiver loses sync.
IDCK setup/hold violation (data not within t_su / t_h relative to IDCK+ edge) — per-pixel sampling error; visible as colour/sync glitches.
TFADJ resistor open or out of 505-515 Ω target — TMDS swing falls outside 400-600 mV; eye degraded.
DKEN trim too large or too small — IDCK ↔ DATA skew exceeds receiver tolerance; pixel data corrupted.
HPD low — display not connected or powered down; source detects via HTPLG and gates TMDS output.
DDC NAK on EDID read (0xA0/0xA1) — display present but EDID corrupted/unsupported; source falls back to default DVI mode.
Receiver not detected (RSEN=0 in DC-coupled systems) — source may gate TMDS output to save power.
Differential clock used in high-swing mode — not recommended per spec (less common-mode noise rejection).
CTL3 driven non-zero — violates HDCP reserved field; receiver may discard or mis-decode blanking.
Pixel data + sync setup violation at full 165 MHz — t_su(IDR) ≥ 1.2 ns / t_h(IDR) ≥ 1.3 ns; violation produces character-encoder error.
Power supply DV_DD out of 3.0-3.6 V — undefined behaviour.
compliance_requirements: TMDS pair count = 3 data + 1 clock = 4 differential pairs.
Pixel rate 25-165 MHz (DVI 1.0); per-channel TMDS bit-rate = 10 × pixel rate (250 Mbps to 1.65 Gbps).
8-to-10b transition-minimised encoding per channel with running DC-balance.
Channel-to-pixel mapping: TX0 = Blue + (HSYNC,VSYNC), TX1 = Green + CTL[1], TX2 = Red + CTL[3:2]; CTL3 always 0 (HDCP reserved).
Single-ended TMDS swing 400-600 mV (R_TFADJ ≈ 510 Ω); differential swing 800-1200 mV pp.
Intra-pair skew t_sk(D) ≤ 50 ps at 165 MHz; inter-pair (channel-to-channel) skew t_sk(CC) ≤ 1.2 ns at 165 MHz.
DVI output clock jitter t_ojit ≤ 150 ps (relative to IDCK).
DVI output rise/fall (20-80%) t_r / t_f = 75 ps min, 240 ps max at 165 MHz.
IDCK duty cycle 30-70%; IDCK clock jitter tolerance ≤ 2 ns.
